subject: Skyline private deployment: maestro plan for cluster slices, networking, and storage binding
content:
From: Alex Tan <alex.tan@skyline.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment intake: Skyline on-prem requirements (initial inventory attached)

Hi Marissa / Laura,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is a quick hardware inventory (Skyline-HW-Inventory.xlsx) and a rough network sketch. High-level asks:
- Customer wants a private (on-prem) Redwood Private deployment behind their datacenter firewall.
- Primary region: single datacenter, 4 racks. Secondary DR site later.
- Workloads: low-latency inference (real-time API) + batch retrain jobs. Expect 3–5m real-time RPS at peak across 8 inference GPUs.
- Storage: need fast local NVMe cache for KV/model cache (ephemeral), and replicated block volumes for model artifacts and logs.
- Security: disk encryption with customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and SOC2 controls.
- Networking: VLANs for control/data/management; strict egress rules; procurement team copied for hardware ordering.

Questions for Redwood: recommended node pool split (inference vs batch vs infra), storage binding pattern (local NVMe + CSI blockstore), control-plane topology for air-gapped vs VPC-connected, and preflight checklist items.

Alex
Skyline AI

----

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@skyline.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment intake: Skyline on-prem requirements (initial inventory attached)

Alex — thanks, this is a great starting point. Quick readout and proposed approach so we can align procurement and engineering: 

1) Control plane
- Recommend HA control plane: 3 control-plane nodes (external load balancer) in primary datacenter. If they need air-gap we can convert the control plane to customer-hosted and run Redwood control plane components as a private control plane appliance.
- Backup plan: daily etcd snapshots pushed to on-prem object store (S3-compatible) + offsite replication to DR later.

2) Node pools (initial MLP)
- infra-pool (3 x m4-sized VMs): kube-system / monitoring / fluentd / CSI controller
- inference-pool (GPU nodes): GPU-optimized servers with local NVMe for KV cache and model shard caching. Taints: gpu=true:NoSchedule; tolerations for runtime pods.
- batch-pool (CPU-heavy): for retraining and offline transforms, scaleable via autoscaler.
- mgmt/utility pool: bastion, control-plane-support, and backup/restore workers.

3) Storage binding pattern
- Local NVMe (ephemeral) mounted on nodes for KV cache (liveness only). Do not back up. Use pod-level nodeAffinity and hostPath or local-static-provisioner with topology-aware scheduling for low-latency.
- CSI-managed block volumes (encrypted) for model artifacts, indices, and logs. Use volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer to ensure correct topology and CSI that supports encryption + KMS.
- PV reclaim policy: Retain for model artifacts (to avoid accidental deletes), Delete for ephemeral test data.

4) Networking / egress
- Recommend Calico for policy enforcement; BGP with route reflectors to advertise podCIDR where possible.
- Egress: NAT gateway per rack or egress IP pools to avoid SNAT on the node level; firewall rules to restrict outbound to approved endpoints (e.g., our telemetry endpoints + customer artifact store).

5) Security & audit
- Integrate with customer KMS (KMIP or cloud-HSM gateway), enforce disk encryption.
- Enable immutable audit logging on control plane and forward to customer SIEM.

Next steps: can we get VLAN tags + desired pod/network CIDRs, and confirm whether the control plane will be reachable from Redwood (managed control plane) or fully air-gapped? Also routing/egress constraints from the network/security teams. I[0m

Attachments: Network-Diagram-v2.png (stub)

Marissa
Principal Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Tan <alex.tan@skyline.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment intake: Skyline on-prem requirements (initial inventory attached)

Quick technical addendum from infra:
- Scheduler & kernel tuning: set massivepages/hugepages for inference containers that use shared memory. Pin CPUs for GPU pods where latency is critical.
- Pod density and eviction: recommend kubelet eviction thresholds at 85% node allocatable for memory and 90% for disk to avoid OOM kills during bursts.
- GPU scheduling: use device plugin and set resourceRequests to avoid overcommit. Add a small burst pool if they expect intermittent XLA jobs.
- CSI recommendations: use a CSI driver that supports volume snapshots + encryption and dynamic provisioning. volumeBindingMode=WaitForFirstConsumer is important for rack-aware volumes.
- Snapshot & backup: Schedule nightly snapshots of model artifacts; replicate to on-prem S3 bucket (retention 30 days) and weekly to DR.
- PV retention: Model artifacts -> Retain; ephemeral logs -> Delete; snapshots -> Lifecycle policy to cold storage after 7 days.

I'll prepare a short preflight checklist (hardware firmware, NIC offloads, iommu, BIOS settings) and share.

Karthik
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Alex Tan <alex.tan@skyline.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@skyline.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment intake: Skyline on-prem requirements (initial inventory attached)

Network gating items from my side:
- IP plan: need rack-level CIDR allocation and desired podCIDR blocks. We prefer /16 for podCIDR at site scale; use /24 per rack for node pools.
- VLAN tags: please confirm VLAN IDs for control, data, mgmt, and storage.
- Firewall: list of allowed outbound endpoints (we will provide an allowlist template).
- BGP details: if we use BGP, provide ASNs and whether RR are in-scope. If not, we will fall back to NAT egress per rack.
- Service egress: telemetry endpoints for Redwood (redacted) plus customer artifact store. We need customer signoff on endpoints to open.

Air-gap question: Alex, does Skyline require total air-gap (no outbound connectivity for control plane)? If so, we will provide an appliance-based control plane that runs entirely on-prem. If Redwood-managed control plane is acceptable, we will need an outbound TLS-only channel through a proxy. Both are supported but timing and procurement differ.

Action needed from Skyline: VLAN IDs, preferred podCIDR, and confirmation of KMS integration method (HSM vs cloud KMS gateway).

Neha
Network Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Thanks everyone — summarized next steps and owners below (MLP = minimum landing product):

MLP (target: 6 weeks)
- Confirm network plan (Skyline): VLAN IDs, podCIDR, and firewall allowlist — owner: Alex (due 2026-06-21).
- Procurement: place order for NVMe-enabled inference servers and a small set of infra nodes (3x control) — owner: Procurement / RackVendor (due 2026-06-25).
- Preflight & firmware checks: Karthik to run checklist against HW once serials available — owner: Karthik (due upon delivery).
- CSI & KMS: Neha to validate CSI driver compatibility with customer KMS; confirm KMIP/HSM handshake — owner: Neha (due 2026-06-24).
- Workshop: 2-hour onboarding workshop (network, storage, canary plan) to be scheduled week of 2026-06-28 — owner: Marissa / Skyline (TBD).

Docs we will deliver:
- Mutual Action Plan (MAP-Skyline-MAP-v1.docx)
- Preflight checklist (firmware, NIC settings, BIOS)
- Runbook: canary rollout steps, rollback playbook, and post-deploy validation queries.

Please confirm acceptance of the MLP items and we[0mll lock calendar for the workshop. If Skyline needs air-gap mode, flag now — that will add ~2 weeks to the timeline for appliance packaging and security review.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
